rationale: Keep Brightspeed active and correct the ownership-scope treatment. Apollo's original acquisition was led by private-equity funds, but the FCC's December 2023 ruling also identifies AIOF II Connect Holdings, L.P. as a direct owner with 2% equity and 3% voting; Apollo identifies AIOF II as a dedicated infrastructure fund. Retain the manager's active ownership period, identify the AIOF II vehicle within the Apollo-managed ownership group and qualify the historical stake because Brightspeed's August 2024 recapitalization issued warrants and preferred stock. Mubadala's May 2, 2023 $500 million minority investment was signed subject to regulatory approvals. The FCC approved the proposed foreign-ownership structure on December 20, 2023, but no public legal-closing announcement or date was found. Retire the unsupported closed-active Mubadala period and record the investment as SIGNED_PENDING_INCOMING through CEPSA Holding LLC. No Apollo or Mubadala exit was found through August 8, 2026.

beforeImage.name: Brightspeed
beforeImage.description: Brightspeed owns and operates wireline telecommunications and fiber broadband infrastructure in the United States. Its customers include residential broadband subscribers, businesses, and wholesale communications counterparties, and the business is investing capital into a largely asset-heavy fiber upgrade program across a legacy local-exchange footprint. Public disclosures describe operations across 20 states and a long-term plan to expand fiber coverage materially within that footprint. The company was formed in connection with Apollo-managed funds' acquisition of Lumen's incumbent local exchange carrier business and launched the Brightspeed brand in 2021 ahead of the transaction close. Mubadala announced a $500 million minority investment in Brightspeed in May 2023. The reviewed public materials do not disclose Mubadala's ownership percentage or the detailed current ownership split among Apollo-managed vehicles.

afterImage.name: Brightspeed
afterImage.description: Brightspeed owns and operates wireline telecommunications and fiber broadband infrastructure across 20 U.S. states from Charlotte, North Carolina. Apollo-managed funds completed the acquisition of Lumen's incumbent local exchange carrier operations in October 2022. FCC records show that the Apollo ownership group included AIOF II Connect Holdings, L.P., a vehicle of Apollo Infrastructure Opportunities Fund II, alongside larger Apollo private-equity and co-invest vehicles. Mubadala signed a $500 million minority investment through CEPSA Holding LLC in May 2023, and the FCC approved the proposed foreign-ownership structure in December 2023; no public legal-closing announcement or date was found, so Mubadala remains a signed pending incoming investor in this census. Brightspeed completed a debt recapitalization in August 2024 that issued warrants and preferred stock, and the current exact ownership percentages are not publicly disclosed. Apollo remained involved after the recapitalization, and no Apollo or Mubadala exit was found through August 8, 2026.

The FCC approved Brightspeed's proposed foreign-ownership structure, including AIOF II's disclosed 2% equity interest and Mubadala's approximately 28% proposed equity interest through CEPSA Holding LLC.

Brightspeed completed a debt recapitalization that secured approximately $3.7 billion of new financing, eliminated approximately $1.1 billion of debt and issued warrants and preferred stock to participating lenders.
